findings.body: The test sets only XDG_CONFIG_HOME, but machine.py:9 selects APPDATA on Windows. After init, line 24 therefore reads a nonexistent temporary registry while Forge writes to the runner's actual config folder. The Windows jobs in .github/workflows/forge-next.yml:23–25 run this test through the suite command at line 36. Set the platform-appropriate config variable so the test both isolates and checks the registry on Windows.
findings.title: Not done: Windows registry command test

findings.body: No test supplies repeated registry lines, a missing checkout, or an existing folder without forge.toml and verifies the reader's result. The current assertions inspect the writer's file contents only. Removing the filtering or dict.fromkeys from machine.py:25–26 would leave this test passing, so the explicitly required reading behavior has no effective coverage.
findings.title: Not done: registry reader filtering and deduplication tests

findings.body: Several command checks pass for unrelated reasons. Sync runs only after init has already registered the checkout, so removing sync from the dispatch registration list would pass. The dry-run assertion also passes if the dry-run guard is removed: _copied_client (tests/test_migrate.py:60–70) supplies no forge.toml in the main checkout, so machine.remember rejects it independently. The refusal check at line 18 likewise uses a checkout without forge.toml. Exercise successful sync with an eligible, unregistered checkout, and exercise dry-run/refusal exclusions where the checkout otherwise qualifies for registration. Each assertion must fail when its corresponding dispatch behavior breaks.
findings.title: Not done: effective command registration and exclusion tests
